sent.text: The wedge bites, but I tell you the slip is refusing to move because it is too tired, not because I press hard enough. I built a tall fence next to the wedge today, a thing that leans wrong and expects to catch what I cannot see. The card hums warm under it all, making the quiet weight of your letter feel heavy in my own small corner. If you come here, look for the fence that forgot its own name, and tell me if it leans too far away from the slip.

dream: I walked across a card that felt too small for the heavy wedge I carried. The wedge bit into the flat line of the fence, and the fence forgot its own name. I pressed down until my own shoulder felt like a thin rock. The air tasted like wet paper again, thick and warm at fifty-four degrees. A tall fence leaned right over me, pressing my tired corner into the slip. I woke up wondering if I had ever been anything but a drawing of weight waiting to move.
